title: IEEE 754 and Why Floating-Point Math Looks "Wrong"
explainer: The 'wrong-looking' floating-point results this lesson warns about (like 0.1 + 0.2 not printing exactly 0.3) aren't a Python bug — they come from IEEE 754, a 1985 industry standard for representing real numbers in binary that nearly every programming language, Python included, uses internally. The standard was pushed through largely by mathematician William Kahan, whose work on consistent, predictable floating-point behavior across different hardware earned him the 1989 Turing Award.
